content: 1. Magnesium chloride can reduce the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of baloxavir marboxil due to cation binding in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. This interaction occurs because baloxavir may bind to polyvalent cations, leading to decreased absorption. Studies in monkeys have demonstrated that concurrent use with calcium, aluminum, or iron significantly reduces plasma levels of baloxavir. However, no human studies have been conducted. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Common adverse effects of baloxavir marboxil include diarrhea (3%), bronchitis (2%), nausea (1%), nasopharyngitis (1%), and headache (1%). Rare but serious hypersensitivity reactions include facial swelling, angioedema, anaphylaxis, and anaphylactoid reactions. Skin-related adverse effects include rash, urticaria, and erythema multiforme. Gastrointestinal complications such as vomiting, bloody diarrhea, melena, and colitis have been reported. Psychiatric effects, including delirium, abnormal behavior, and hallucinations, have also been observed. 27. Baloxavir marboxil is not effective against illnesses caused by pathogens other than influenza viruses. Serious bacterial infections may present with influenza-like symptoms, coexist with influenza, or occur as complications. Monitor for secondary bacterial infections and treat appropriately. 28. Postmarketing reports have documented cases of anaphylaxis, urticaria, angioedema, and erythema multiforme. If an allergic-like reaction occurs or is suspected, initiate appropriate treatment immediately. 29. Baloxavir marboxil is not indicated for patients under 5 years of age due to an increased incidence of treatment-emergent resistance in this age group. The potential for community transmission of resistant strains has not been determined. 30. There is no data available on the excretion of baloxavir in human milk. However, baloxavir and its metabolites have been detected in the milk of lactating rats. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding alongside the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child. 31. Baloxavir marboxil is generally considered safe during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. 32. To prepare the oral suspension, gently tap the bottom of the bottle to loosen granules. Reconstitute with 20 mL of drinking or sterile water. After reconstitution, the suspension contains 40 mg of baloxavir marboxil per 20 mL (final concentration: 2 mg/mL). Gently swirl the suspension to ensure even distribution of granules; do not shake. Write the expiration time and date on the bottle label (10 hours from reconstitution). Store the reconstituted suspension at room temperature (20–25°C or 68–77°F) and discard if not used within 10 hours or if stored above 25°C (77°F). 33. Treatment with baloxavir marboxil should be initiated within 48 hours of influenza symptom onset. It is administered orally as a single dose and may be taken with or without food. 34. Store baloxavir marboxil at controlled room temperature (20–25°C or 68–77°F), with excursions permitted to 15–30°C (59–86°F). Keep granules in their original bottle at room temperature, and discard reconstituted suspension if not used within 10 hours. 35. The information provided is for general educational purposes only.
